Jubile
jū´bĭ-lē
n. (the fiftieth year of release; rendering Hebrew yobel)
From Hebrew yobel, a ram's horn — the year is named for the trumpet that announced it. The KJV spells it with one l.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The jubile is the fiftieth year, when Israel's land returned to its families and her slaves went free: “ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession” (Lev 25:10). The economics rest on a stated theology: “The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me” (Lev 25:23). Isaiah 61's acceptable year of the LORD draws on it, and Christ read that passage in Nazareth and said it was fulfilled.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines jubilee as among the Jews, every fiftieth year, being the year following the revolution of seven weeks of years, at which time all the slaves were liberated and all lands reverted to the former owner.

expand to see more

JUBILEE, n. Among the Jews, every fiftieth year, being the year following the revolution of seven weeks of years, at which time all the slaves were liberated, and all lands which had been alienated during the whole period reverted to their former owners.

2. A season of great public joy and festivity.

Key Scripture

Lev 25:10 — "And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family."

Lev 25:23 — "The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. for"

Isa 61:1 — "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;"

Luk 4:21 — "And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears."

Modern Corruption

Jubilee is treated as a quaint agrarian rule or a political slogan, while its actual claim — that no one finally owns land, because God does — is unwelcome in every economy.

expand to see more

Leviticus 25:23 is the sentence that makes the whole institution intelligible: the land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Israel's real estate transactions were therefore leases, not sales, priced by the number of harvests remaining until the jubile. Permanent dispossession was structurally impossible, because a family's inheritance could be temporarily lost but never finally alienated. That is not agrarian nostalgia; it is a theology of ownership with an accounting system attached.

Luke 4 is where the trumpet finally sounds. Christ reads Isaiah's proclamation of liberty to the captives and the acceptable year of the LORD, closes the book, and says this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears. The jubile was always a rehearsal for a release from a deeper debt, and the congregation that heard the announcement tried to throw Him off a cliff — which is roughly how every settled economy receives the news that the land was never theirs.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yobel (H3104), ram's horn, and by extension the year its blast announced; the trumpet sounded on the day of atonement to open it.

expand to see more

Hebrew yobel (H3104) — ram's horn, jubile; Leviticus 25:9-13, Numbers 36:4.

Hebrew deror (H1865) — liberty, release; Leviticus 25:10, proclaim liberty throughout all the land.

Greek aphesis (G859) — release, remission; Luke 4:18, to preach deliverance to the captives.

Usage

"“Proclaim liberty throughout all the land” — the fiftieth year opened by a horn."

"“The land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me” — the theology under the economics."

"“This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears” — the trumpet sounded in Nazareth."
